CheckGpuDriverOld: Over a year old. Newer drivers often fix stutter and add game optimizations. Official source:
CheckRefreshLow: Your display supports {0} Hz at this resolution. Raising it in Settings › Display › Advanced display is the single biggest smoothness improvement available.
CheckGameModeDetail: Prioritizes the game and pauses Windows Update installs while you play.
CheckHagsDetail: Needed for DLSS Frame Generation. Otherwise the effect is small and GPU-dependent.
CheckRecordingDetail: Continuously records the last minutes of gameplay, which costs GPU encoder time and disk writes.
CheckPowerLaptop: On a laptop, Balanced lets the CPU boost while keeping battery life and temperatures in check.
CheckWindowedOptDetail: Lets borderless DirectX 10/11 games use the low-latency flip model.
CheckDualChannelDetail: One memory stick runs in single-channel mode. A second matching module can noticeably raise FPS in CPU-bound games, especially with integrated graphics.
CheckMemorySpeedLow: Your modules are rated {0} MT/s. Enabling XMP/EXPO in the BIOS is usually the fix (this app never changes BIOS settings).
OverlaysIntro: Overlays hook into games. One is fine; several at once can cause stutter or crashes.
GamingHonesty: There is no registry setting that adds meaningful FPS on a healthy Windows 11 system. Real gains come from the refresh rate, drivers, memory configuration, thermals and the game's own settings — so that's what this page checks first.
GamingTweaksIntro: Each setting shows what it changes, why, its downsides and how to undo it. Recommendations depend on your hardware.
WhatSlowsDown: What is slowing this PC down
CheckBackgroundCpuDetail: Measured over 2 seconds. Above ~6% at idle usually means a program is busy in the background.
CheckCommitDetail: How much of RAM + page file is promised to programs. Near 100% causes slowdowns and "out of memory" errors.
CheckStartupDetail: Each app that starts with Windows delays sign-in and uses memory in the background.
CheckHddDetail: Mechanical drives are the most common cause of a slow PC. Moving Windows to an SSD helps more than any setting.
CheckPendingRebootDetail: Updates are waiting for a restart. Some may run in the background until you restart.
Symptoms:
Slow to start → too many startup apps, HDD, pending updates.
Stutter in games → low refresh rate, background recording, overlays, old GPU driver, thermal throttling.
Everything feels slow → memory pressure (high committed memory), HDD, background CPU.
Mouse feels laggy → pointer acceleration, low refresh rate, wireless interference.
Apps freeze at random → failing disk (see Repair › Disk health), driver crashes (see event logs).

ResetNetworkDetail1: Static IP addresses and custom DNS servers will be lost.
ResetNetworkDetail2: Some VPN and security software may need to be reinstalled.
ResetNetworkDetail3: A restart is required. This cannot be undone by the app.

ResetNetworkAck: I understand my custom network settings will be lost.

BenchmarkExplain: Run once before changing anything and once after. Each metric has a noise threshold: differences inside it are reported as "within noise", not as an improvement.

BenchmarkTip3: A 512 MB temporary file is written to the temp folder and deleted afterwards.
NoiseNote: Synthetic tests can't measure game FPS directly. Use them to confirm a change didn't make things worse, and check FPS in your own games.

PrinciplesText:
• Nothing changes without your review and consent.
• Every change records the original value and can be undone.
• Windows Defender, Firewall, UAC, SmartScreen and Windows Update are never disabled.
• Personal files are never deleted; deletion is always previewed.
• Drivers and firmware are never downloaded or flashed.
• Recommendations depend on your hardware; dangerous changes are never recommended.

Page_security_Sub: Microsoft Defender status and scans, plus a review of the places malware hides
SafeSetIntro: Only low-risk changes that match your hardware and are not applied yet. You see the full list and can untick anything before it runs; a restore point is created first.
AllOptimizationsIntro: Each entry says what it changes, why, the expected effect and the drawbacks. Nothing here claims more FPS without evidence.
ServicesIntro: Most Windows services start only when needed and use little memory. Disabling them rarely speeds anything up and often breaks a feature later. Only the few services listed as changeable can be modified here, after a restore point, and every change is undoable.
NeedsAdminServices: Run Windows Ultimate as administrator to change a service.
SvcWhy_Essential: Windows needs this service to start, sign in, connect or update. Changing it can leave the PC unusable.
SvcWhy_Security: Part of Windows protection (Defender, firewall, updates, credentials). Windows Ultimate never disables these.
SvcWhy_KeepDefault: Often listed in “debloat” guides, but its default setting already costs almost nothing, and disabling it breaks a feature.
SvcWhy_Optional: An optional Windows feature. It can be changed if you do not use it.
SvcWhy_ThirdParty: Installed by another program. Manage it from that program or uninstall the program; disabling it here can break it without warning.
SvcWhy_Unclassified: A Windows service with no documented reason to change it. It is left as Windows set it.
SvcVerdictChange: Can be set to {0} if you do not use it.
SvcVerdictThirdParty: Managed by the program that installed it.
SvcRestartNote: Takes effect after a restart. Undo from this page or from History.
SecurityDisclaimer: Windows Ultimate is not an antivirus and does not replace one. Microsoft Defender (or your antivirus) gives the verdicts. The security check below looks for indicators: an indicator means “worth a look”, not “malware”. Nothing is deleted or moved without your confirmation.
DefenderActive: Defender is active and real-time protection is on.
DefenderRealtimeOff: Defender is active but real-time protection is off. Turn it back on in Windows Security.
DefenderInactive: Defender is not active and no other antivirus was found.
DefenderUnavailable: Defender status could not be read on this PC.
ProtectedByOther: Protected by {0}. Defender scans are handled by that antivirus.
SignaturesOutdated: Defender is active but its signatures are out of date.
OfflineScanTip: Restarts the PC into Microsoft Defender Offline to scan before Windows loads. Use it only when you suspect malware that hides from normal scans.
DefenderWorking: Defender is scanning. You can keep using the PC.
FullScanRunning: Full scan running… This can take an hour or more.
FullScanMessage: Defender reads every file on every drive. It can take an hour or more and slows the PC while it runs. You can cancel it at any time.
ScanThreatsFound: Defender found {0} threat(s). Review them below.
ScanClean: Scan finished in {0:0.#} min. Defender found nothing.
SignaturesUpdated: Defender signatures are up to date.
SignaturesUpdateFailed: The signature update did not complete. Try again from Windows Security.
OfflineScanMessage: The PC restarts within a minute and Microsoft Defender scans it before Windows loads (about 15 minutes). Save your work first.
OfflineScanDetail1: Open programs are closed; unsaved work is lost.
OfflineScanDetail2: Results appear in Windows Security › Protection history.
OfflineScanAck: I saved my work. Restart now.
RemoveThreatsMessage: Microsoft Defender applies its own remediation to the active detections below (quarantine or removal). You can restore quarantined items from Windows Security.
SecurityCheckIntro: Reviews startup entries, scheduled tasks, services, browser extensions and settings, running programs and high-risk folders for signs of info-stealers, backdoors or hijacks. Read-only: nothing changes until you choose an action.
SecurityNotRunYet: Not run yet. It takes about a minute.
SecurityTrustedHidden: {0} item(s) you marked as trusted are hidden.
NeedsAdminSecurity: Without administrator rights some places cannot be read (other users, Defender exclusions, some services). Run as administrator for a complete check.
NoFindings: No indicators found in the places checked. This does not prove the PC is clean: run a Defender scan as well.
TrustCleared: Trusted items forgotten. They will show again on the next check.
RemedyNotApplicable: Nothing to change any more: the item is already gone or disabled.
LookupTitle: Look up this hash on VirusTotal?
LookupMessage: Your browser opens VirusTotal’s page for this SHA-256 hash. Only the hash is sent; the file itself is never uploaded.
TrustMessage: This item is hidden from future security checks. Defender still scans it. You can undo this at the bottom of the page.
EndProcessMessage: {0} (PID {1}) is running from this file. It has to stop before the file can be moved to quarantine. Unsaved work in it is lost.
PersistenceInventoryIntro: Startup entries, tasks, services and hooks reviewed by the check, flagged or not.
ExtensionInventoryIntro: Installed extensions and the powerful permissions they hold (reading every site, cookies, downloads…). A permission is not a verdict.
SpeedTestNote: Runs only when you click, against {0} (Cloudflare), and uses up to {1} MB of data. Results depend on your line, router, Wi-Fi, other devices and server load: one run is a sample, not a verdict.
BufferbloatTip: Extra latency while the line is busy. High values mean games and calls lag when someone downloads; the fix is usually SQM/QoS on the router, not a Windows setting.
CompareFirst: First speed test on this adapter. Run another after a change to compare before and after.
CompareWith: Compared with {0}: download {1}, upload {2}, ping {3}, bufferbloat {4}. Differences of a few percent are normal noise.
NetworkRecommendationsIntro: Based on your adapters, settings and the tests you ran. A change is suggested only when a measurement or a known misconfiguration supports it; none can guarantee a lower ping.
DnsProviderIntro: DNS turns names into addresses. A faster resolver makes the first connection to a site quicker; it does not change download speed or in-game ping. Switching is undoable and restores your previous servers.
MtuRunning: Measuring the largest packet that passes unfragmented…
MtuFailed: The MTU probe got no replies (ICMP may be blocked).
RssTip: Receive Side Scaling spreads network processing over several CPU cores.
Ipv6LocalOnly: Local only (your provider or router does not offer IPv6)
MeasurementHistoryIntro: Your last tests, stored on this PC only. Run one before and after a change to see its real effect.
ClearMeasurementsMessage: All saved speed and ping results are deleted from this PC.
ConnectionsIntro: Which programs have network connections open right now (IPv4 TCP). Useful to find what uses the connection during a game.
ClearNetworkCachesDetail: Flushes the DNS cache; as administrator also the ARP and NetBIOS caches. Harmless; fixes sites that moved to a new address.
CachesAdminNote: Only the DNS cache can be cleared without administrator rights.
WindowsTroubleshootersDetail: Microsoft’s own guided fixes for network and internet problems.
NoSpeedTestYet: No speed test yet. Measure before changing anything.
ExecutionLogIntro: Every command and change Windows Ultimate ran, as written to its log file (kept 90 days on this PC).
